$comment: Inventory of the tools available on this machine, for an agent working over Bash. Derived from modules/nixos/packages.nix + modules/home/default.nix — those files are the source of truth; this one is a reading aid. Deliberately carries no version numbers: run `<tool> --version` instead, which is always current. Update after changing the package lists.
$schema_notes: This file is checked mechanically by ~/.claude/check-conventions.sh — keep these contracts true or the check fails.
tools[].commands — the executables the entry puts on PATH. Omitted means `[name]`. An empty array means the entry ships no binary under its own name (a bundle or a library).

tools[].package — the nixpkgs attribute or home-manager program name. Must appear in modules/nixos/packages.nix or modules/home/default.nix. null means the entry is not separately declared under its own attribute — the base system, or a command a service option puts on PATH; purpose says which.
not_installed[].names — every command the entry covers, one per element. This is the machine-readable field; there is no `name` here on purpose, so the list cannot drift from its prose.

tools[].agent_unsafe — commands that hang a session with no terminal. Optional; present only on the interactive entries. Each element is {command, forms}, where forms is "all" or "bare". "all" generates BOTH a bare and a `<name> *` deny — the bare form matters, because ` *` alone does not match the argument-less command that is actually typed. "bare" generates ONLY the exact match, for a tool whose subcommands are scriptable and must stay available: `codex` hangs, `codex exec` does not, and emitting `codex *` would deny the useful half while missing the form that hangs. Claude takes these declaratively and Codex through a hook, from this one array, so adding an interactive tool here denies it for both. Use a multi-word prefix as the command where the tool needs one, so only the hanging subcommand is denied and the scriptable siblings stay available. Nothing declares one at present — zellij did, and was removed — but the field is what makes that expressible without hand-writing a rule beside this file.

machine.shell: fish (default login shell); bash is present for scripts
machine.config_repo: /etc/nixos (git, branch main; owned by the user via tmpfiles — no sudo needed to edit)

env.EDITOR: nvim — interactive sessions only, and set on jj's ui.editor as well as the variable, so `jj describe` does not depend on which shell launched it. Agent sessions pin JJ_EDITOR/GIT_EDITOR/EDITOR/VISUAL to `false` via managed settings, so a command that would open an editor fails fast instead of hanging on a full-screen one. That guard does not cover jj's diff editor (bare jj split, jj diffedit, jj resolve without --list or --tool mergiraf), which is a builtin TUI.

notes: Impermanence is enabled: only declared/persisted paths survive a reboot. Do not leave state in the home root.

Build parallelism is derived from machine.threads and machine.memoryGiB (modules/nixos/machine.nix), not hand-set — this host lands on max-jobs 2 x cores 6 because RAM is the binding constraint. Do not raise it by hand; change machine.memoryGiB and let the formula follow.
Installing software imperatively does not work here. Add the package to modules/nixos/packages.nix and run `nh os switch /etc/nixos`, or use `nix shell nixpkgs#<pkg>` for a one-off.

tools.name: rg
tools.purpose: Fast recursive regex search over file contents.

tools.name: fd
tools.purpose: Fast file/directory search by name.

tools.name: jq
tools.purpose: JSON query and transformation.

tools.name: git
tools.purpose: Version control. Kept because jj uses it as its backend and gh speaks it.

tools.name: jj
tools.purpose: Jujutsu VCS over the git backend — colocated repos, no staging area, `jj undo` on any operation.
tools.notes: Bare `jj` is configured to show the log. `git.colocate` and `git.track-default-bookmark-on-clone` default to true; `git.auto-local-bookmark` no longer exists. No version is named here on purpose: check-conventions.sh asserts all four claims against `jj util config-schema` and `jj config get`, so they go red when one stops being true rather than when jj is upgraded.

tools.name: jjui
tools.purpose: TUI over jj's operation log. Interactive — do not launch from an agent shell.

tools.name: gh
tools.purpose: GitHub CLI — PRs, issues, `gh api`.
tools.notes: Auth is per-user state; check `gh auth status` before assuming it is logged in.

tools.name: nix
tools.purpose: Flakes-enabled Nix. `nix shell nixpkgs#<pkg>` for a throwaway tool, `nix build`, `nix flake`.

tools.name: nh
tools.purpose: NixOS rebuild wrapper: `nh os switch /etc/nixos`, `nh os boot`, `nh clean`.
tools.notes: nh declines to run as root — run it as the user. /etc/nixos is user-owned, so that works without sudo; the git safe.directory entry is a leftover guard, no longer load-bearing.

tools.name: nixd
tools.purpose: Nix language server (used by the editor, not usually called directly).

tools.name: statix
tools.purpose: Nix linter. `statix check <path>`, `statix fix`.

tools.name: nixfmt
tools.purpose: Official Nix formatter. Reachable directly, but in /etc/nixos prefer `nix fmt`, which runs it under treefmt with this repo's exclusions applied.

tools.name: nix-index
tools.purpose: `nix-locate bin/<name>` says which package ships a file — the lookup step behind "a missing tool is a decision", without guessing attribute names.
tools.notes: The database is prebuilt and declared (nix-index-database, wired in modules/nixos/home-manager.nix). Never run `nix-index` to build one: it writes to ~/.cache/nix-index, which impermanence does not persist, so the work is lost at reboot and shadows the declared copy until then.

tools.name: comma
tools.purpose: Run a program without installing it: `, <cmd>` resolves it through the same nix-index database nix-locate reads, fetches the package and runs it. The one-off route of law 1 collapsed into one step; leaves nothing behind.

tools.name: devenv
tools.purpose: Per-project development environments (devenv.nix). This is where language toolchains live — including Rust via languages.rust, and mold via languages.rust.mold.enable.

tools.name: direnv
tools.purpose: Auto-loads a project's devenv shell on cd. Fish integration is enabled. Declared as `programs.direnv` in modules/home/default.nix, with `nix-direnv.enable = true` alongside it.
tools.notes: A non-interactive agent shell may not have the project env loaded — run `direnv exec . <cmd>` if a project tool appears missing.

tools.name: uv
tools.purpose: Python package/project manager. `uv run`, `uv sync`, and `uvx <cli>` for one-off Python CLIs.
tools.notes: There is no system-wide python3 on this machine — uv is the only way to get a Python interpreter.

tools.name: sccache
tools.purpose: Compiler cache. Wired in globally via RUSTC_WRAPPER so devenv shells inherit it.
tools.notes: `sccache --show-stats` to confirm cache hits. A cache hit is the cheapest way to survive the RAM ceiling.

tools.name: docker
tools.purpose: Rootful Docker daemon, on PATH because virtualisation.docker.enable is set in modules/nixos/winboat.nix — winboat drives a dockur/windows container through docker-compose. Not a package in packages.nix, and not an invitation: a container is not the route around law 1 for a tool nixpkgs already has. docker-compose is not on PATH system-wide; winboat's wrapper suffixes its own.

tools.name: shellcheck
tools.purpose: Shell script linter. Run over any sh/bash script you write here.

tools.name: shfmt
tools.purpose: Shell formatter — the other half of shellcheck. `shfmt -d <file>` shows the diff, `shfmt -w` applies it.

tools.name: typos
tools.purpose: Source and prose spell checker with an identifier-aware dictionary — near-zero false positives, which is why it is gated in `nix flake check` here rather than advisory. `typos --format brief <path>`; exit 2 means findings; `--write-changes` fixes in place.
tools.notes: Run it over anything you write before calling it finished — this machine's output is mostly prose-carrying config that no human proofreads. Its first run on this tree caught a real typo in agent-denies.nix.

tools.name: hyperfine
tools.purpose: Statistical benchmarking of shell commands — a performance claim without hyperfine numbers is an assertion, not a result. `hyperfine --style basic --export-json out.json 'cmd A' 'cmd B'`; `-N` skips the shell for hot-path timing; `-w` adds warmup runs.
tools.notes: `--style auto` already drops the progress bar without a TTY, but NO_COLOR is ignored — pass `--style basic` in agent shells.

tools.name: deadnix
tools.purpose: Finds unused bindings and function arguments in .nix files. Run it as `deadnix . -e ./hosts`.
tools.notes: Third of three passes that do not overlap: nixfmt formats, statix lints idioms, deadnix finds what nothing uses. Two traps. `--exclude` is variadic and swallows the positional argument, so `deadnix -e ./hosts` scans nothing at all and reports success — give the path first. And `--edit` rewrites files with no regard for which are generated: it stripped an unused `pkgs` from hosts/*/hardware-configuration.nix, an edit that file forbids and that nixos-generate-config would undo. Read the findings and fix them by hand.

tools.name: moreutils
tools.purpose: Small shell utilities. `sponge` is the one that matters: `jq '…' f | sponge f` edits a file in place, where `jq '…' f > f` truncates it before jq reads it.
tools.notes: The package also ships a `parallel` that is NOT GNU parallel and takes different flags — it is left out of `commands` here on purpose, so nothing in this inventory points an agent at it. `vidir` and `vipe` open $EDITOR: agent-unsafe, see the editor guard.

tools.name: yq
tools.purpose: jq's query language over YAML (`yq`), TOML (`tomlq`) and XML (`xq`). Use instead of sed for structured config — a workflow file, a devenv.yaml.
tools.notes: This is the python wrapper (kislyuk), deliberately not `yq-go`: it takes jq syntax, so there is no second query language on this machine. A `yq` example found online may be written for yq-go and will not parse. This is also why yq is declared despite being barely invoked — four packages ship /bin/yq (yq-go, yq, python3xxPackages.yq) and yq-go sorts first, so `, yq` would hand you the incompatible one. The declaration is what pins which yq.

tools.name: file
tools.purpose: Identify an unknown blob by content rather than extension.

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.purpose: Secret scanning. `gitleaks detect` / `gitleaks git` before pushing.
tools.notes: This config repo is public — scan before committing anything that touches identity or credentials.

tools.name: eza
tools.purpose: Modern ls replacement (`eza -la`, `eza --tree`). Aliased over ls/ll/la/lt/lla in interactive fish, so a user's `ls` is eza — but the aliases do not reach a non-interactive agent shell, which still gets coreutils `ls` and its parseable output.

tools.name: fzf
tools.purpose: Fuzzy finder. Interactive — needs a TTY; not useful non-interactively.

tools.name: herdr
tools.purpose: Agent multiplexer, and since 2026-08-27 the terminal one too — it is Alacritty's shell (modules/home/default.nix), so a window arrives already inside a session. A background rust server keeps coding-agent sessions alive independently of the terminal that launched them, marking every pane working / blocked / idle; bare `herdr` launches or attaches to the ONE persistent session, so two windows are two views of it rather than two sessions. It replaced zellij, which multiplexed panes in one window and died with it. Prefix key is F12 rather than upstream's ctrl+b (herdr/config.toml), because vim wants <C-b>. Config in ~/.config/herdr, state in ~/.local/state/herdr, worktrees in ~/.herdr — all three persisted (modules/nixos/impermanence.nix). Subcommands (`herdr tab`, `herdr pane`, `herdr agent`, …) are scriptable; only the bare word is a TUI. Upstream ships a `curl | sh` installer; nixpkgs carries it, so law 1 needs no exception.
tools.notes: Bare `herdr` starts or reattaches the TUI and hangs a session with no terminal, so it is agent_unsafe with forms "bare": `Bash(herdr)` is denied and `Bash(herdr *)` is not. Every subcommand stays available, which is the point — `herdr agent list/read/prompt/wait`, `herdr pane`, and the socket API behind `herdr api` are how an agent is meant to drive it. This entry was dropped on 2026-08-25 when the field could only deny both forms at once, because walling off the CLI cost more than the hang did; forms made the narrow rule expressible and it came back the same day. A skill teaching the CLI is generated from `herdr --skill` at build time and linked into ~/.claude/skills/herdr and ~/.codex/skills/herdr (modules/home/skills.nix) — one source, so it cannot drift from the binary. Its HERDR_ENV=1 gate is close to vestigial now that herdr is Alacritty's shell (since 2026-08-27): every terminal window arrives already inside a pane with the variable set, so the gate excludes only what is not a terminal at all — a cron run, a cloud agent. What keeps the skill from firing unasked is its description, which limits it to sessions naming Herdr explicitly, and that description is its standing cost — roughly ninety tokens in every session's prompt whether or not the skill is invoked, with only the body deferred until it is.

tools.name: alacritty
tools.purpose: GPU terminal emulator. GUI.

tools.name: neovim
tools.purpose: LazyVim on Neovim. The config is declared in /etc/nixos/nvim and symlinked into ~/.config/nvim; the plugins are runtime state under ~/.local/share/nvim/lazy, persisted but not declared. Its toolchain (gcc, nodejs, unzip, tree-sitter) is on neovim's wrapper PATH only and does not reach a terminal. Interactive — do not launch from an agent shell.

tools.name: claude
tools.purpose: Claude Code CLI.
tools.notes: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR points at /home/mehti/.claude so its state lands in a persisted directory under impermanence.

tools.name: codex
tools.purpose: OpenAI's coding agent. Bare `codex` opens an interactive TUI and will hang a session with no terminal — `codex exec` is the non-interactive form. Its instructions are ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, a store symlink generated from claude/CLAUDE.md so both agents read one source.
tools.notes: Bare `codex` opens an interactive TUI; `codex exec` is the non-interactive form. That distinction is why agent_unsafe entries carry `forms`: this one is "bare", so it generates `Bash(codex)` and NOT `Bash(codex *)`, which would have denied the safe subcommand. Before forms existed the field could only say "both patterns", so this rule was hand-written into modules/nixos/agent-denies.nix instead and the inventory said the tool was safe — the field lying while a note beside it told the truth. Its walls are /etc/codex/requirements.toml, generated by modules/nixos/codex.nix from the guards in agent-guards.nix and the deny list in agent-denies.nix. Two rules are thinner there than for Claude: shellcheck-on-write does not port (apply_patch reports tool_input.command, not a file_path), and the spill rule keys on a path shape not yet observed in a real Codex payload.

tools.name: brave-origin
tools.purpose: Browser. GUI. Binary is `brave-origin`, not `brave`.

tools.name: obsidian
tools.purpose: Markdown notes over a local folder of plain files. GUI, so an agent shell cannot drive it — read and write the vault's .md files directly instead.
tools.notes: Unfree (Obsidian EULA); allowUnfree is already set in modules/nixos/nix.nix. The vault is ordinary markdown on disk and is NOT persisted by virtue of being a vault: keep it under ~/Documents or ~/Projects, which impermanence.nix lists. ~/.config/obsidian is covered by the wholesale .config entry.

tools.name: prismlauncher
tools.purpose: Minecraft launcher. GUI.
tools.notes: PrismLauncher-Cracked fork (github:Diegiwg/PrismLauncher-Cracked), overlaid to replace the official nixpkgs package — supports offline accounts only. The fork exists to bypass purchase verification, so a real Microsoft account is unsupported and risks violating Mojang/Microsoft ToS.

tools.name: steam
tools.purpose: Valve's game client and store. GUI, so an agent shell cannot drive it. Declared through programs.steam (modules/nixos/steam.nix) rather than systemPackages, because the bare package cannot run: Steam ships and downloads prebuilt 32-bit binaries that expect FHS paths, and the module is what provides the sandbox those resolve in.
tools.notes: Reverses the 'Not installed, on purpose' entry POST-INSTALL.md carried from the beginning. Rides on two settings that were already true and are not restated in steam.nix: nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree (nix.nix) and hardware.graphics.enable32Bit (hardware.nix), the second being the usual reason a fresh install renders nothing. Remote Play and dedicated-server firewall ports, the gamescope session and extraCompatPackages are all deliberately left off; steam.nix says why for each. State is ~/.local/share/Steam for the library and ~/.steam for the login, both in impermanence.nix.

tools.name: winboat
tools.purpose: Windows apps on Linux: a dockur/windows container running a real Windows VM under KVM, with an Electron front end that pulls individual app windows onto the Plasma taskbar over RDP. GUI, so an agent shell cannot drive it — and first run is a multi-hour unattended Windows install, not a command that returns.
tools.notes: Needs the rootful docker daemon and the docker group, both set in modules/nixos/winboat.nix, and /dev/kvm, which systemd's stock udev rules ship 0666. Carries a permittedInsecurePackages entry for its EOL electron-40.10.5 — the exact version string, so a nixpkgs bump fails loudly rather than widening the exception. State lives in ~/winboat (the Windows disk image, 32 GiB minimum), ~/.winboat (compose file, app list, guest credentials) and /var/lib/docker (the image and the container) — all three are in impermanence.nix, and losing any of them means installing Windows again.

tools.name: fish
tools.purpose: Default interactive shell.
tools.notes: Fish is not POSIX. `&&`/`||` work, but `$(...)` subshell quirks, `export`, and array syntax differ — write scripts for bash and run them with `bash script.sh`.

tools.name: coreutils-and-friends
tools.purpose: Base-system commands, always present. `curl` lives here — there is no wget.
tools.notes: Not a nixpkgs attribute of its own, hence package: null. The bundle name is not itself a command; the `commands` array is what exists on PATH. rsync and strace ride in via NixOS's environment.defaultPackages rather than any list in this repo — present by default, listed here so the inventory stops under-promising what PATH actually holds.

not_installed.workaround: Use `uv run` / `uvx`. No system interpreter exists.
Per-project via devenv (`languages.javascript`), or `nix shell nixpkgs#nodejs`.
Deliberately absent system-wide so it cannot shadow project toolchains. Use devenv's `languages.rust`.
Not on PATH outside a nix shell. Use `nix shell nixpkgs#gcc nixpkgs#gnumake` or a devenv shell.
Not enabled. Docker is — see .tools; it is rootful and exists for winboat. podman would have to be talked through /dev/kvm and RDP port binding, which winboat does not support.
`nix shell nixpkgs#unzip -c unzip <file>`. `tar` handles .tar.* archives; a plain .zip needs unzip — there is no bsdtar on PATH, despite what this entry used to claim.

`, ast-grep …` runs it for one command, or `nix shell nixpkgs#ast-grep -c`. Dropped 2026-08-24 after 0 invocations in 10,354 recorded commands: this tree is nix, markdown and a little bash, which rg covers. Note `sg` is util-linux's setgid wrapper and always was — it is not ast-grep.
`, btop`, or Plasma's own System Monitor, which is installed and was the reason btop went unused. Dropped 2026-08-24.

`, sticky`. Dropped 2026-08-24: its notes.json held an empty list, obsidian does the same job and is actually used, and it pulled mate-panel in behind Mint's xapp for +188 MiB. `xpad` is the +5 MiB equivalent if a floating pad is ever wanted again.

`, bat` — only bat.out ships /bin/bat, so there is no ambiguity to resolve the way there is for yq. Dropped 2026-08-24 after 0 invocations in 10,591 recorded commands: it was enabled but nothing ever called it, since no PAGER, MANPAGER or fzf preview named it. `less` is the pager and `nvim` opens what wants highlighting.

Skip it, deliberately — its option database evaluates stock modules only and cannot see this flake's custom options. The covered routes: `nix eval` over nixosConfigurations.<host>.options (sees everything, custom options included), `nh search options` (NixOS + home-manager scopes, --json), `man home-configuration.nix` for offline HM docs, noogle.dev by web for lib functions. Evaluated 2026-08-25.

Deferred until a project actually gates on SAST — 696 MiB closure and useful only with vendored local rules. When borrowed: `nix shell nixpkgs#semgrep -c semgrep scan --config <local-rules-dir> --metrics=off --disable-version-check --error --quiet --sarif .` — NEVER `--config auto`, which fetches the registry and sends telemetry on every run, and logged-out output redacts fingerprints. opengrep is the cleaner engine (LGPL, no telemetry) but is not in nixpkgs. Evaluated 2026-08-25.

`nix shell nixpkgs#mergiraf -c jj resolve --tool mergiraf` on a merge conflict — jj already ships the merge-tool config, so this needs zero setup. Syntax-aware: auto-merges what it can prove safe (nix, bash, yaml, toml, json among others). Trust its warning output and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'`, never the exit code — jj swallows mergiraf's; what stays marked is hand-edited, the CLAUDE.md route. Evaluated 2026-08-25.

`nix shell nixpkgs#hurl -c hurl --test api.hurl` — HTTP assertions as a plain file with a real exit code, the mechanical way to prove an API behaves instead of eyeballing curl output. A project that adopts .hurl suites pins hurl in its own devenv.nix.

`nix shell nixpkgs#duckdb -c duckdb -c "SELECT ..."` for CSV/parquet/sqlite/large-JSON analysis — one SQL engine instead of csv-tool sprawl. ALWAYS pass `-c`: bare duckdb is a REPL and hangs a session with no terminal.

`nix shell nixpkgs#pandoc nixpkgs#typst -c pandoc in.md -o out.docx` — only for PRODUCING docx/pptx/pdf for humans; never borrow it to read, agents read PDFs natively. PDF goes through `--pdf-engine=typst`, never the multi-GiB TeX route.

conventions: Never install with a package manager — edit modules/nixos/packages.nix (system) or modules/home/default.nix (user), then `nh os switch /etc/nixos`.
For a tool needed once, `nix shell nixpkgs#<pkg> -c <cmd>` leaves no trace.

In /etc/nixos: `nix fmt` formats the tree, `nix flake check` gates it. Formatting is treefmt's alone, configured once in treefmt.nix — do not invoke nixfmt or shfmt directly there, or the repo's exclusions are skipped. The check runs formatting, deadnix, statix and shellcheck, plus evaluation of every host. jj has no hook support and bypasses .git/hooks entirely, so the gate cannot be a git pre-commit hook — a Claude Code PreToolUse hook runs it on `jj commit` and `jj git push` instead (modules/nixos/claude.nix). gitleaks runs from the same hook on a wider set — `jj new`, `jj squash` and `jj split <paths>` too, since in jj those make working-copy content permanent as `@-` rather than creating a commit, so a secret is past the point of amendment before any push.

statix is gated, with four house-style lints turned off in statix.toml at the repo root (repeated_keys, manual_inherit, manual_inherit_from, empty_pattern) — the disagreement was a configuration problem, and leaving it unconfigured meant every OTHER statix lint went unenforced too. The file is undotted on purpose: statix auto-discovers `statix.toml` and not `.statix.toml`, so a by-hand `statix check .` behaves exactly like the gate.

One thing `nix flake check` does not cover: installer.sh is exempt from shfmt. It has never been formatted, needs 256 lines changed at any indent width, and partitions disks and shreds an encryption keyfile, so reformatting it is a deliberate decision rather than a side effect. shellcheck still covers it.

hosts/*/hardware-configuration.nix is generated by nixos-generate-config and excluded from every nix linter — it carries a real unused argument whose only fix the file forbids, a permanent false positive. Running deadnix by hand: the path comes first, `deadnix . -e ./hosts`, because --exclude is variadic and swallows the positional, so `deadnix -e ./hosts` silently scans nothing and exits 0.
`nh` and `git` run as the user, never as root. /etc/nixos is already user-owned, so edits need no sudo.

Service CLIs follow the gh model: the human auths once with a long-lived scoped token (env or machine.secretsDir, never a browser flow that expires), agent-hostile defaults are disabled declaratively (AWS_PAGER="", WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false, CLOUDSDK_CORE_DISABLE_PROMPTS=1 and their kin), and a CLI is installed only when the service is actually in use — plain CRUD against a stable REST API is curl plus a bearer token, not a wrapper CLI.

Never start a dev server in the foreground — it holds the shell and the session with it. `devenv up` runs a project's processes supervised under process-compose, which devenv already bundles: logs land in files, and nothing spawns a duplicate server.
